title: Parts of the body
subtitle: head, hand, knee, foot
summary: Name the parts of the body, inside and outside, and use my, your, his and her with them correctly.

lesson.heading: Head and face
rows: It grows on top of your head.
You eat and speak with it.
They are inside your mouth. An adult has 32.
It joins your head to your body.

lesson.heading: Arms and legs
rows: at the top of your arm
between your shoulder and your hand
at the end of your arm; it has five fingers
the short, thick finger on your hand
on the end of every finger and toe
in the middle of your leg
at the end of your leg; it has five toes

lesson.heading: The rest of the body
lesson.text: The front of your body is your **chest** and your **stomach**. The other side is your **back**. In the middle you have your **waist** and your **hips**, and on the left and the right is your **side**.

examples.text: I have a pain in my **side**.
She wears a belt around her **waist**.
He carries the bag on his **back**.

lesson.heading: Inside the body
lesson.text: You cannot see these parts, but you need them every second: your **heart**, your **brain** and your **blood**.

examples.text: The **heart** is a symbol of love.
Your **blood** type can be A, B, AB or O.

lesson.heading: Singular and plural
lesson.text: Two body words have a special plural: one **foot** - two **feet**, and one **tooth** - two **teeth**. **Hair** is a singular, uncountable word, so it takes *is* and *it*.

examples.text: That woman has got very big **feet**.
The baby has already got two **teeth**.
My **hair is** dirty. I need to wash **it**.
examples.wrong: My hairs are dirty. I need to wash them

lesson.heading: my, your, his, her
lesson.text: With parts of the body we usually use **my**, **your**, **his**, **her** and so on - not *the*.

examples.text: I have a pain in **my** leg.
The little girl needs to wash **her** face and **her** hands.
examples.wrong: wash the face and the hands

lesson.heading: Body words inside other words
rows: a comfortable chair with a place for each arm
the game you play with your feet
colour that people put on their lips
you brush your hair with it
a scarf you wear on your head
a small bag for your money, keys and phone

lesson.text: Learn the two strange plurals as a pair: *one foot - two feet*, *one tooth - two teeth*.

exercises.explanation: Four fingers and a thumb - together we call them five fingers.
The small parts at the end of your foot are toes.
Your nose is in the middle of your face.

exercises.prompt: Match each part of the body with what it does.

pairs.right: it is a symbol of love
its type can be A, B, AB or O

exercises.prompt: Put each word in the right part of the body.

exercises.statement: That woman has got very big foots.
exercises.explanation: That woman has got very big feet. The plural of foot is feet.

exercises.statement: The little girl needs to wash her face and her hands before dinner.
exercises.explanation: Correct. We use her, not the, with parts of the body.

options: My grandfather has a pain in his shoulder.
My grandfather has a pain in the shoulder.
My grandfather has a pain in shoulder.
My grandfather has a pain in a shoulder.
exercises.explanation: Use my, your, his, her with parts of the body.

exercises.statement: My hairs are dirty. I need to wash them.
exercises.explanation: My hair is dirty. I need to wash it. Hair is a singular word.

exercises.prompt: Your side hurts. Tell the doctor.
exercises.answer: I have a pain in my side.
exercises.explanation: a pain in my side - not in the side.

exercises.prompt: A comfortable chair with a place for each arm is an ___.
